record.paper_title: Open problems on billiards and geometric optics
record.original_question: Let γ be a planar oval, and for any chosen pair of directions define F: γ → γ by moving from a point x along a line in the first direction to the next intersection with γ and then along a line in the second direction to the next intersection point. If for every pair of directions the map F is conjugate to a rotation, must γ be an ellipse?

evidence.quote: Question 1: Is this property characteristic of ellipses?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let γ ⊂ ℝ² be a planar oval (a smooth, strictly convex closed curve). For any ordered pair of directions (u, v) ∈ S¹ × S¹, define a map F_{u,v} : γ → γ as follows: for x ∈ γ, draw the line through x in the direction u and let y be the next intersection point of this line with γ (other than x); then draw the line through y in the direction v and let F_{u,v}(x) be the next intersection point of this line with γ (other than y). Suppose that for every choice of directions (u, v) for which F_{u,v} is well defined as a self-map of γ, the map F_{u,v} is conjugate to a rigid rotation of the circle. Must γ be an ellipse?
artifact.status_search_result: The question belongs to a circle of rigidity problems characterizing ellipses through dynamical/projective properties of associated maps on the curve. The closely related Birkhoff–Poritsky conjecture and conjugacy-rigidity questions for convex billiards remain open in full generality (only partial results, e.g. for nearly circular or locally integrable domains, are known). No source found announcing a proof of this specific characterization, so it appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Nearly circular domains which are integrable close to the boundary are ellipses
status_evidence.snippet: The Birkhoff–Poritsky conjecture states that an integrable convex billiard table must be an ellipse; only nearly circular cases are resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Related ellipse-rigidity conjectures for convex billiards remain open in general.

status_evidence.title: On conjugacy of convex billiards
status_evidence.snippet: If two billiard maps are conjugate near the boundary the domains are similar; full rigidity results are conditional.
status_evidence.claim: Conjugacy-based ellipse characterizations are an active but unresolved area.
